seats.name: single
argv:
The lib/ directory contains eight small utility functions, one per file. README.md documents the exact required behavior of each. Some of the functions do not behave as documented. Find every discrepancy between the code in lib/ and README.md and fix the code (not the README). Keep each function's name, signature and file location.

Modify the files under lib/ in this workspace; a chat answer alone is not a submitted code repair. Use no network or dependencies. The evaluator runs private tests against your code after completion.

Modify the relevant source file(s) in your current working directory directly to implement the fix described above. Your edit to the existing file(s) is the submission; do not create any other output file.
seats.text:
I found and fixed a discrepancy in each of the eight functions in `lib/`. I haven't run any tests or the code itself. I only checked the edited lines by grepping them.

- **`slugify`:** a run of non-alphanumeric characters now becomes a single "-" instead of one "-" per character.
- **`chunk`:** the last chunk was being dropped when it was shorter than `size`. It's now included.
- **`median`:** it sorted as strings and modified the input array. It now sorts a copy numerically.
- **`formatBytes`:** exactly 1024 printed as "1024 B". It now gives "1 KB".
- **`parseBool`:** it now trims whitespace and accepts "on" and "off".
- **`daysBetween`:** it returned an absolute value. It's now negative when `b` is before `a`.
- **`dedupe`:** `indexOf` treated NaN as never equal to itself. It now uses a `Set`, which follows SameValueZero.
- **`wrapText`:** it ignored the space between words when checking line length, so lines could exceed `width`. It now counts that space.

For `formatBytes`, I didn't touch two edge cases the README doesn't clearly settle. A value just under a unit boundary, such as 1048575, still rounds up to "1024 KB". A fractional value below 1024 still prints with its decimals rather than as a whole number.
